newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-De La Rue sees long term growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-De La Rue sees long term growth.

text.p: British printing and security products group De La Rue Plc on Tuesday ruled out any immediate surge in its performance but promised medium- to long-term growth on current investments being made in its cash systems and smart card divisions.
The company disappointed investors on Tuesday by reporting pretax, pre-exceptional profits of 120.2 million stg against 147.9 million in the previous year.
The share price tumbled 52 1/2 pence to 432 1/2 with analysts blaming the hammering on the lower-than-expected performance figures.
Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits in a range between 124.0 and 129.5 million stg.
De La Rue's chief executive Jeremy Marshall, however, said that this was a temporary phase and the company needed at least another couple of years before it could show steady growth.
"We are taking the pain now in order to build on a stronger platform," Marshall told Reuters in an interview.
Marshall pencilled the company's investments in cash systems and smart card divisions as its main future vehicles for growth.
"Sales of newly-developed products are expected to increase, particularly towards the end of the financial year," Marshall said.
He said the division's profit was expected to grow during the current year.
Adverse exchange rates and lower sales on products with higher profit margins had pulled down the company's operating profits from this division to 22.1 million stg from 38.0 million.
The company is investing a significant portion of its expenditure on developing 20 new cash systems products. "We are pretty sure about very good returns from them," he said.
"One would expect the volumes to pick up in a couple of years," he said.

The company expects to invest more in developing the cash systems market in some of the emerging economies like India, China, the Ukraine, Poland and Russia, currently witnessing sweeping banking reforms including automation.
The company is also banking on its recent 54 million stg acquisition of Philips Smart Cards and Systems.
De La Rue's forecasts, Marshall said, was that the smart card market would treble from a 1.0 billion today to more than 3.0 billion by the turn of the century.
"We have a very clear strategy and we believe that the investments we are making now will give us very good growth in the medium-term future," Marshall said.
